quote_zh: A mixture of enol ester (20g, 0.06mol) and dichloromethane (60mL) taken in a clean, pre-dried 250mL round bottomed flask and cooled to 10-15°C. To this mixture, added sodium cyanide (1.2g, 0.025mol) followed by slow addition of triethylamine (6.6g, 0.065mol) for 15-20mins at 10-15°C under stirring. The reaction mixture is cooled at 10-15°C and maintained for about 2 hours and quenched with water (100mL). Dichloromethane was separated through distillation under reduced pressure at 35-45°C. The aqueous mass obtained was cooled to 5-10°C and acidified to pH < 3 using aqueous hydrochloric acid (5.4mL, 0.054mol). The precipitated product obtained was separated through filtration, washed with water (60 mL) and dried under reduced pressure to obtain mesotrione as yellow to tan colour solid. HPLC purity >95%; Yield: 17g (85%); Melting point of the solid was 155-157°C;and solvent recovery: > 85%.
arithmetic_check:
Four printed quantity pairs, plus a printed product mass and yield. Every pair is consistent with the compound named once the precision of the printed mass is propagated, and the printed mass and yield close on the true molar basis, so no arithmetic flag is raised. Nothing was corrected.

ENOL ESTER, CLOSES. The drawn reactant SMILES CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)OC2=CC(=O)CCC2)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1 gives C14H13NO7S, MW 339.325 by RDKit. 20 g is therefore 20 / 339.325 = 0.058941 mol. The page prints 0.06mol, which is that value at the two decimal places printed; the rounding window for 0.06 at two decimals runs 0.055 to 0.065 mol, implying 307.7 to 363.6 g/mol, and 339.325 sits inside it.

MASS BALANCE, CLOSES EXACTLY. The drawn product SMILES CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)C2C(=O)CCCC2=O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1 is also C14H13NO7S, MW 339.325; reactant and product are isomers, which the vision pass noted independently as a consistency check on its own two readings. So on the true molar basis: in 20 / 339.325 = 0.058941 mol, out 17 / 339.325 = 0.050100 mol, yield 0.050100 / 0.058941 = 85.0%, against the printed 85%. It closes to three significant figures. Two further observations. First, because the molecular weights are identical the theoretical maximum output mass equals the input mass, 20 g, and the printed 17 g is below it, so there is no impossibility of the kind mass_balance_implausible exists to catch. Second, if the yield is instead computed against the patent's own ROUNDED input figure of 0.06 mol, it comes out as 0.050100 / 0.06 = 83.5%, which would round to 84% and not to the printed 85%; that 1.5 point gap is an artefact of the patent rounding 0.058941 up to 0.06 in print, not a defect in the mass and yield it reports, and the true molar basis above is the one that governs. mass_balance_implausible NOT raised.

TRIETHYLAMINE, CLOSES. 6.6 g at 101.19 g/mol for C6H15N is 0.065224 mol, which rounds to the printed 0.065 mol at three decimals.

SODIUM CYANIDE, A BOUNDARY CASE, resolved as CONSISTENT and NOT flagged, with the reasoning set out in full because the sibling records flag pairs of a similar percentage deviation. 1.2 g at 49.007 g/mol for NaCN is 1.2 / 49.007 = 0.0244862 mol. Rounded once to the three decimals the page prints, that is 0.024, whereas the page prints 0.025, and the implied molecular weight of the printed pair, 1.2 / 0.025 = 48.0 g/mol, is 2.1% below the true 49.007. Taken naively that looks like the Example 1 NMST case, which DID earn molar_mass_inconsistent at a 2.2% deviation. It is not, and the distinction is the precision of the printed MASS, which has to be propagated rather than ignored. 1.2 g is printed to two significant figures, so the mass it stands for lies in 1.15 to 1.25 g, and the mole figure it implies lies in 1.15 / 49.007 = 0.02347 to 1.25 / 49.007 = 0.02551 mol. The printed 0.025 mol sits inside that interval, so the printed pair is consistent with the compound named to the precision at which the patent prints it, and asserting a defect here would be asserting more precision than the page carries. The same propagation applied to the sibling cases does NOT rescue them: Example 1 prints 61.2 g, an interval of 61.15 to 61.25 g, implying 0.28412 to 0.28458 mol, which excludes the printed 0.278 entirely; Example 3 prints 20 g, an interval of 19.5 to 20.5 g, implying 0.0906 to 0.0953 mol, which excludes the printed 0.088 entirely. So the test is uniform across the four pairs and separates them cleanly, rather than being special pleading for this one. Two secondary observations point the same way. First, the computed 0.0244862 mol rounds at four decimals to exactly 0.0245, the half-way value, which then rounds up to the printed 0.025, so a two-stage rounding reproduces the printed figure exactly; no rounding path of any kind reaches Example 1's 0.278 or Example 3's 0.088. Second, the gap between the computed value and the 0.0245 rounding boundary is 0.0000138 mol, 0.06% of the boundary, against gaps of over 2% in window terms for the two flagged pairs. On that basis molar_mass_inconsistent is NOT raised. The contrary reading is recorded rather than suppressed: a reviewer who applies the rounding-window test to the printed mole figure alone, without propagating the mass precision, would find 0.0244862 outside the 0.0245 to 0.0255 window and would raise the flag. Nothing else in the record turns on it either way, since the sodium cyanide is sub-stoichiometric and enters no mass balance.

ENOL ESTER AND TRIETHYLAMINE UNDER THE SAME MASS-PRECISION TEST, both consistent, recorded so the test is seen applied to every pair and not only to the awkward one. 20 g of enol ester stands for 19.5 to 20.5 g, implying 0.05747 to 0.06041 mol, and the printed 0.06 mol is inside it. 6.6 g of triethylamine stands for 6.55 to 6.65 g, implying 0.06474 to 0.06572 mol, and the printed 0.065 mol is inside it.

HYDROCHLORIC ACID, NOT MOLECULAR-WEIGHT CHECKABLE. 5.4 mL with 0.054 mol is a solution volume against a mole figure, implying 10.0 mol per litre. That is plausible for a concentrated aqueous hydrochloric acid, about 32% w/w, but the text prints no concentration and no density for it, so there is no mass of substance to divide and no molecular weight check is possible. Not flagged. WATER likewise carries volumes only, 100mL for the quench and 60 mL for the wash, with no mole figure.

STOICHIOMETRY, computed here but deliberately NOT written into the record, since the patent states no equivalents and molar_ratio_text is null: on the printed 0.06 mol of enol ester, sodium cyanide is 0.42 eq, triethylamine 1.08 eq and hydrochloric acid 0.90 eq. The sub-stoichiometric cyanide is the fact behind the catalytic-versus-ionic mechanism note on the record.

SCALE CONTINUITY. Not testable as a step-to-step comparison, because no precursor step is asserted. For the record, the three sections that make this reactant report 25.4 g (Example 4, line 302), 0.89 g (Example 5, line 310) and 22.8 g (Example 6, line 318). A 20 g charge is available from Example 4 or from Example 6 and is not available from Example 5's 0.89 g. This narrows the three candidate precursors to two but selects neither, and mass sufficiency is weaker evidence than the name similarity that prompt rule 24 already refuses to treat as confirmation, so precursor_step stays null and scale_discontinuity is not raised.

PURITY IS A MEASUREMENT REPORTED AS A BOUND. Line 331 prints "HPLC purity >95%" with no space after the sign, for the single batch this Example made, so product_purity_pct is 95.0 with purity_method hplc, understood as the printed lower bound and not an assayed equality; the inequality is kept verbatim in procedure_text, in the quote above and in A1's raw_text for the same compound. "Yield: 17g (85%)" is a measurement and both numbers are recorded. "solvent recovery: > 85%" is a property of the dichloromethane, not of the product, and is recorded in prose only: byproduct_recovery is scoped by prompt rule 14 to by-products and the dichloromethane is the reaction solvent, and that block has no field meaning recovery percentage, only concentration_pct, which would misfile the number. The melting point 155-157 C has no field on a reaction record and lives on the A1 compound.
drawing_evidence:
The scheme IMAGE_EXTRACT at line 327 is the only such span inside lines 320-332 and is this section's own. p18.json records it as kind "scheme", between_markers [null, "[0053]"], presented_as "invention_route", the only drawing on the page, occupying the whole top of the page above [0053] with nothing between it and the running header but the centred page number. The null first marker is correct and not a failure: the Example 7 heading and sub-title that introduce the scheme fall on the preceding printed page, so there is no earlier marker on this page to anchor it to. One left-to-right arrow, one reaction record.

AGREES WITH THE PROSE ON STRUCTURE AND CONNECTIVITY. Reactant CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)OC2=CC(=O)CCC2)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1, C14H13NO7S, labelled "Formula II" on the drawing, is the enol ester the prose charges. Product CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)C2C(=O)CCCC2=O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1, also C14H13NO7S, labelled "Formula I", is the mesotrione the prose obtains. Both SMILES are the ones A1 carries as aliases on those two compounds, so the drawing, the prose and A1 name the same two molecules. The vision pass read the ring positions off the drawn hexagons rather than inferring them: both benzene rings are drawn vertex-up and identically substituted, NO2 at the top vertex, the acyl carbon at the top-right vertex, the sulfonyl at the bottom-left vertex; in the left structure the ester oxygen sits between the aryl carbonyl and the ring carbon bearing the C=C, so the enol oxygen is 1,3 to the ketone. Both structures come out as the same formula, so the drawing depicts an isomerisation, which is the basis for the rearrangement reading of reaction_class recorded on the record. The two labels are printed without parentheses, "Formula II" and "Formula I", unlike the "formula (III)" style the prose uses elsewhere in the document; the roman numerals were re-read at 6x because the broken ink makes I and II easy to miscount.

THE ARROW IS BARE, AND THIS IS THE LARGEST DRAWING-VERSUS-PROSE GAP IN THE DOCUMENT. reagents_above and reagents_below are both empty lists. This was not an eye reading: p18.json records that the 190 pixel wide band spanning the arrow was scanned for dark pixels over 390 rows above and below, and the only ink found was the arrow line itself at rows 447-457, the wide rows 453-454 being the arrowhead. So the labels are genuinely absent from the page rather than merely unread, which is the distinction between a bare arrow and an unread one and matters because a guard must not pass on absence. The arrow looks finely dashed at 4x but is a degraded solid line with one filled arrowhead pointing right; the dash pitch on it matches that on every C-C bond in both structures, which identifies it as broken ink rather than a drawn dashed arrow.

CONSEQUENCE. Every scheme for step (iii) in this patent is drawn this way, so the prose at line 329 is the sole source in the document for this step's solvent, reagents, temperature, hold time, quench, distillation and acidification. p18.json's own discrepancies list records the same thing as its first entry. Five materials are named in the procedure and appear on no arrow anywhere in the document: sodium cyanide, triethylamine, dichloromethane, water and aqueous hydrochloric acid. reagent_written_not_drawn is raised on that basis and covers all five. drawing_text_conflict is deliberately NOT raised: a bare arrow asserts nothing and therefore contradicts nothing, and the drawn structures match the written names atom for atom. This is the same line Example 1 drew for its "Oxidant / RuO2" arrow, and a conflict flag on a drawing that does not contradict its prose would send a reviewer to look at a non-finding.

TWO FURTHER VISION DISCREPANCIES, RECORDED AND NOT FLAGGED. p18.json's second entry notes that neither "Formula I" nor "Formula II" appears in any text on this page, so on the evidence of page 18 alone the identification of the drawn structures with the named compounds rests on the drawing; the sub-title at line 322, on the preceding page, does connect them by reading "Synthesis of mesotrione from enol ester of formula (II)", so the gap is a page-boundary artefact rather than a real ambiguity in the document. Its third entry notes that the product is drawn in the keto form, with plain single bonds from the benzoyl-bearing carbon to both flanking carbonyls and no OH anywhere, checked at 6x specifically for a doubled line on either bond, while the prose states no tautomer and reports only a melting point and a colour, so which tautomer the isolated solid is cannot be settled from this page. Neither is a disagreement between the drawing and the prose, so neither raises a flag.

ROUTE ATTRIBUTION. Not in question. The vision pass set presented_as "invention_route" and the scheme stands inside an Example under the EXAMPLES heading, drawing step (iii) of the invention's own three-step route. route_attribution_unclear is not raised. NMSBC, the acid chloride of the four-step prior art of US 7,820,863, appears nowhere in this section or in this drawing.

LINKAGE EVIDENCE FROM THE DRAWING. None, and that is the point. The scheme draws the enol ester as a free-standing structure on the left of the arrow with no indication of which earlier Example produced it, and there is no multi-arrow scheme on this page connecting it back to NMSBA. So the drawing cannot break the three-way tie between Examples 4, 5 and 6, and precursor_step stays null with linkage_confirmed false. The A2 records for all three of those sections were on disk when this record was written and all three carry product_name "enol ester of formula (II)", identical to this step's reactant identifier, so the tie is confirmed as a genuine three-way one and not an artefact of a missing file: reaction_ids Example 4_Step 1, Example 5_Step 1 and Example 6_Step 1 are equally good candidates on identifier match, which is exactly why identifier match cannot choose among them. None of the three names Example 7 anywhere in its own record, so there is no forward claim to reconcile either.
